title: Unified bound for binary search trees
formal:
Does there exist one uniform deterministic online binary-search-tree program \(A\) in the model below and one integer \(C\ge1\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge1\), every integer \(m\ge0\), and every request sequence \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in[n]^m\), the program correctly completes all requests and
\[
T_A(n,X)\le C\bigl(n\log_2(n+2)+U_n(X)\bigr),
\qquad
U_n(X)=\sum_{t=1}^{m}\log_2\!\left(2+\min\left\{n,\min_{1\le s<t}(t-s+|x_t-x_s|)\right\}\right)?
\]
Here \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), an empty minimum is \(+\infty\), an empty sum is zero, and \(T_A\) includes initialization and all computation. The same program, its fixed storage constants, and \(C\) must work for all \(n,m,X\). The guarantee is total amortized cost for every finite sequence, including every finite prefix, with no worst-case bound on an individual request.
definitions:
There is exactly one node for each key in \([n]\). Each node has an immutable key and parent, left-child and right-child pointers, any of which may be null. At all times these pointers describe one rooted binary tree in symmetric order: every key in a left subtree is smaller than its root key and every key in a right subtree is larger. An access to \(x\) must visit its node with the cursor and signal completion before the next request is revealed. The cursor starts at the current root for each access. There are no key insertions or deletions during the request sequence.

The program has finite control and fixed positive integers \(c,d,r\). A word has exactly \(w=d\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\) bits. Each node has \(c\) additional mutable words; outside the tree there are at most \(r\) word registers, a root pointer and one cursor. The constants and program are independent of \(n,m,X\). The input supplies \(n\) and then one key at a time; it supplies neither \(m\) nor a free time counter. Registers may retain data between accesses. Earlier requests are accessible only through this charged state. There are no other memory records, random bits, advice, or oracles.

The following instructions each cost one unit: copy a word or a program constant into a register; compare two unsigned words; add, subtract or multiply words modulo \(2^w\); unsigned integer quotient or remainder, returning zero when the divisor is zero; bitwise Boolean operations; logical shifts, with a shift by at least \(w\) giving zero; and conditional or unconditional branching. Each instruction has only a fixed finite number of operands. Reading the current node's key or one of its additional words, writing one of its additional words, and testing one of its three pointers for null each cost one unit. The finite instruction set is fixed; there is no instruction for arbitrary functions of a word. Root and cursor pointers cannot be converted to words, ordered or computed arithmetically. A numerical key or a number stored in metadata cannot be used as a memory address.

Moving the cursor along one parent or child edge costs one unit. A rotation between the current node and its nonnull parent costs one unit, updates the usual constant number of structural pointers, preserves symmetric order, and leaves the cursor at the same key. These are the only changes to the tree during accesses. Reading another node's key or metadata requires moving the cursor there; rotations do not provide free access to that metadata. There are no auxiliary pointer fields, persistent fingers, arbitrary node jumps or cursor resets during an access. At the start of each access, receiving its key and placing the cursor at the root is one charged instruction; acknowledging successful completion is another. A null-edge move, invalid rotation, premature acknowledgement, or broken tree invariant is an incorrect execution.

Initialization precedes all requests, sees only \(n\), and counts toward \(T_A\), also when \(m=0\). It starts with no nodes and zeroed registers except the input \(n\). Only during this phase, a unit-cost allocation instruction may create a zeroed node with a supplied key as the root of an empty tree or as a null left or right child of the current node, placing the cursor at the new node. Each allocation must preserve symmetric order; at most \(n\) nodes may be allocated, and no nodes are reclaimed. The other instructions and storage restrictions remain as above. Initialization must terminate with all keys present in the canonical balanced tree \(B_n\): for an interval \([a,b]\), its root is \(\lfloor(a+b)/2\rfloor\), its left subtree recursively represents \([a,\lfloor(a+b)/2\rfloor-1]\), and its right subtree represents \([\lfloor(a+b)/2\rfloor+1,b]\); an empty interval has no node. Any initialized metadata and registers must be computed by the same program at charged cost. Thus neither constructing the initial tree nor preprocessing is free.

The bound uses elapsed access indices \(t-s\), exactly as in Definition 2 of the 2024 source. It does not substitute the number of distinct intervening keys. For \(t\ge2\), taking \(s=t-1\) shows that the inner minimum is at most \(n\), so the cap has no effect. When \(m\ge1\), the \(t=1\) term is \(\log_2(n+2)\); the source omits that term, which is absorbed by the initialization allowance. Logarithms and indices in the displayed bound are mathematical quantities, not free machine operations.

This fixes the existing card's bounded-storage BST interpretation as a real-world BST with all local computation charged. The classical geometric BST cost counts touched nodes or cursor moves and rotations, and can leave the computation choosing those operations uncharged; its bounds are not automatically full-runtime bounds in the model fixed here.
why: The unified bound asks one search tree to exploit temporal and rank locality together, beyond separate working-set and dynamic-finger guarantees. Resolving whether that combined access bound is achievable would clarify a central limit of adaptive binary search trees.

context_blocks.text: The 2024 paper states the elapsed-access version of the unified bound and reports \(O(U_n(X)+m\log\log n)\) BST access bounds, apart from initialization. Its conclusion explicitly retains the question of removing the extra per-access term.

The real-world BST definition uses a constant number of logarithmic-bit registers and logarithmic extra bits per node. The card makes this storage convention and the cost of local computation explicit; it does not transfer a geometric access-cost theorem to full runtime without an implementation proof.

Derryberry's thesis claimed a BST achieving the unified bound. Iacono's 2013 survey describes that claim as potentially faulty, and the 2024 paper again calls it questioned. The 2011 workshop abstract itself claims success; it is not a published correction or an independently verified resolution.

A preprint dated 14 April 2026 introduces a different unified bound for heaps and still says that no BST achieving the search-tree unified bound is known. Its positive tree result permits arbitrary internal remodeling and leaves outside sorted order, so it does not meet this card's BST model. The preprint's proofs were not independently verified.

progress.text: Iacono's survey records doubts about the earlier BST claim and distinguishes geometric access cost from implementable real-world BSTs.
The ICALP paper uses the elapsed-access definition, reports the additive \(O(m\log\log n)\) overhead and explicitly retains the full unified-bound question.
A later primary preprint on unified-bound heaps again distinguishes its heap result from the unresolved BST bound.
Rechecked the source definitions, the older claim and the later heap result; specified uniformity, word storage, charged local computation, canonical initialization and the full negation.

answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean proof of the stated existence claim, including the uniform program, fixed storage constants, initialization, online correctness and total cost bound, or a complete Lean proof of its full logical negation. The negation says that for every candidate program with every allowed choice of its fixed storage constants and every integer \(C\ge1\), there exist \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(X\in[n]^m\) for which initialization or a request fails to finish correctly, or \(T_A(n,X)>C(n\log_2(n+2)+U_n(X))\). Refuting one proposed tree, bounding only restricted sequences, or proving a conditional lower bound does not establish this universal nonexistence claim. The Lean theorem must use precisely the stated elapsed-access bound, storage and computation model.
status_note: Source-open: ICALP 2024 explicitly retains the elapsed-access unified-bound question, and arXiv:2604.12653v1 of 14 April 2026 again reports that no BST with the unified bound is known. The earlier cache-splay claim is questioned in the checked 2013 and 2024 sources; the 2026 positive result concerns a different heap model. A bounded review through 16 September 2026 found no verified resolution. The card fixes an explicit real-world implementation model with charged computation; geometric access-cost bounds alone do not establish its full-runtime guarantee.

sentences: The unified bound makes an access inexpensive when its key is close in rank to a recently accessed key.

The target is total cost within a constant factor of that bound plus one initialization allowance.
The fixed program uses a constant number of logarithmic-bit fields and registers, and all local computation is charged.
